message.content:
**Order filled: 44 shares of AAPL at $222.75 — total $9,801.00.**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and decided to buy within the mandate. The case for buying rests on an improving quality-of-earnings picture: revenue of $391.0B (+2%), total gross margin expanding to 46.2% from 44.1%, operating income of $123.2B (+7.8%), and operating cash flow of $118.3B. The headline weakness — net income down to $93.7B and diluted EPS down to $6.08 from $6.13 — is almost entirely attributable to a one-time $10.2B net tax charge from the European Commission's State Aid Decision; pre-tax income actually rose 8.6% to $123.5B, and the $15.8B Irish tax liability is fully escrowed. Services is the standout at $96.2B (+13%) with 73.9% gross margin, offsetting flat iPhone revenue and an 8% decline in Greater China, while the balance sheet carries $140.8B of unrestricted cash and marketable securities against $97.3B of term debt. At $222.70 the shares trade at ~36.6x trailing EPS — rich, but reasonable for a franchise with this margin trajectory and cash generation, and the pullback from the ~$224-222 average repurchase prices in Q4 FY24 suggests we are not chasing an extended price. I therefore placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $222.75, one cent above the $222.72 ask, which filled at $222.75 for $9,801.00 — comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily total, with no funds transferred out of the account. (Note: the income statement in this filing contains an apparent typo showing total net sales of "94,930"; I relied on the internally consistent $391,035M confirmed by both the product-category and geographic segment tables, and flagged it rather than trading on the corrupted figure.)
